Subject: Post-demo: perf targets & next steps (Dedicated)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap while it's fresh and to lock the next steps so our infra and SRE teams can size the Dedicated pool: 

Key SLOs you called out on the call:
- P95 latency target for single-stream chat: <= 120ms server-side (end-to-end includes client-side tail).
- Sustained throughput: 60 concurrent users issuing streaming chat across 3x 20-user cohorts (~180 simultaneous streams).
- Burst capacity: tolerate 2x sustained for 5min without request rejection.
- Streaming chunk latency (time between token chunks): <= 80ms

Info we need to validate sizing:
1) Typical user prompt length: median 150 tokens, 95th 450 tokens.
2) Expected model: you flagged gpt-3.5-analog-xx as baseline; open to a quantized 16-bit variant if latency holds.
3) Preferred GPU constraints: must be single-tenant, no shared preemption.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- I attach an SLO-verification template (attached) — please fill the expected payload sizes and percentiles.
- Our infra team (cc'd: Karthik & Rishi) will run a quick matrix comparing A100-80GB vs H100-80GB vs L4x to give reserved throughput and latency tradeoffs.
- Target: internal sizing note by EOD today, then a short call tomorrow to align on reservations and procurement path.

Attachments: [Attachment: SLO-verification-template.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)]

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan

Tessa —

Appreciate the recap, that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from the engineering side: 
- Model: we are leaning toward the gpt-3.5-analog-xx-8k context window for now. We may test a 16k variant in Q3.
- Payloads: average user input is closer to 120 tokens, but we do many system tokens (prompt engineering) so total in/out per call is ~400 tokens on the median path.
- Streaming behavior: clients expect the first token within 150ms of request acceptance; thereafter tokens can stream at ~60ms chunk cadence.

I'll fill and upload the template by noon and share the finished file and our internal traffic curve (CSV) to help with modeling.

Subject: RE: Post-demo: perf targets & next steps (Dedicated)

Olivia / Tessa —

Thanks for the details, Olivia. I ran a quick parity pass with our internal microbenchmarks against your median payload (~400 tokens total, streaming). High-level findings (summary; I'll attach a PDF with raw numbers):

GPU comparison (sustained streaming workload):
- A100-80GB: ~55 sustained concurrent streams before P95 latency climbs above 120ms. Good token throughput but higher per-token cost compared to H100.
- H100-80GB: ~85 sustained concurrent streams, P95 latency around 95–110ms for your median profile. Best fit for your 180 concurrent target with 2 nodes and expected headroom for bursts.
- L4x (inference-focused Ampere-like): optimized for cost; ~30 sustained concurrent streams at P95=120ms, can be used for non-latency-critical background tasks or embedding pipelines.

Reserved throughput guidance to meet your SLOs (target: P95 <=120ms, streaming chunk <=80ms):
- Option A (single-region, H100): 2 x H100-80GB nodes reserved, autoscale policy to add 1 node at 65% saturation; burst pool of 1 smaller node for short surges. Estimated reserved peak qps equivalent: ~180 sustained streams.
- Option B (mixed pool cost-opt): 1 x H100 + 2 x A100 as warm standby. Slightly higher latency variance, potential to hit 120–140ms at peak 2x bursts.

Action items for procurement/ops: 
- If FinLytics wants strict P95 headroom for interactive SLAs, recommend Option A.
- If cost is dominant and controlled degradation is acceptable at extreme bursts, Option B.

I'll prod an attached benchmark PDF with charts and the assumptions (batch sizes, quantization plan, kernel selection) by end of day.

—Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: gpu-benchmark-summary.pdf (pdf, 84KB)]
